text: The memory-nonlinearity tradeoff (Dambre et al. 2012) says that within a reservoir's fixed total capacity budget of N:
choices: linear memory and nonlinear computation add independently, each able to reach N at the same time
capacity spent on nonlinear processing is capacity taken away from linear memory, since C_linear + C_nonlinear <= N
increasing nonlinearity simultaneously raises both linear and nonlinear capacity
the total capacity N can be exceeded by adding more nonlinearity
explanation: The total information-processing capacity is conserved at <= N and is split among degrees, so raising nonlinear (degree >= 2) capacity necessarily reduces linear memory C_1 and vice versa. They cannot both reach N at once, more nonlinearity does not boost linear memory, and no amount of nonlinearity lets the total exceed N.
